extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, students of short-story technique, short-story writers, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and critical standards for judging short stories and short-story collections (style, technique, characterization, plot, translation, unity, etc.), as evident in a yearbook-style review of many recent volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic achievement may fail when an author over-emphasizes a social gulf or other singular idea at the expense of craft (e.g., 'fail in artistic achievement because of their excessive realization of the gulf between the two races').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting a single ethical/political emphasis overwhelm artistic form; strive for balance between subject-matter and artistic control. Anti-pattern: stories that are thematically correct but artistically unconvincing because the theme drowns technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy versus artistic distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree and manner of sympathy toward characters matters: 'Mrs. Martin's book is the more artistic and the less sympathetic, though it has more professions of sympathy than that of Mr. Means.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professions of sympathy are not the same as artistically effective portrayal; sympathetic stance can weaken artistry if it replaces precise depiction. Consider whether apparent sympathy serves the story's artistic aims or merely asserts a position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent in historical portraiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to render historical periods convincingly (e.g., 'considerable talent... in historical portraiture of reconstruction times').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accuracy of period detail, integration of historical context into character and plot, and whether the portraiture serves emotional and dramatic needs. Example: successful historical studies warrant close attention from students of technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genial caricature and humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of genial caricature to portray particular social types or 'the more childish side' of groups can be a valid technique when it produces infectious humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor must be matched to the author's abilities and the material; anti-pattern: humor that relies on stereotypes without insight. Evaluate whether caricature illuminates character or merely mocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative richness / poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaginative capacity or its lack ('suffers from a certain imaginative poverty') is a detectable quality that affects a writer's range and freshness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for originality in images, ideas, and moral imagination. 'Imaginative poverty' is implicated when material is stale or restricted by cultural/puritanical limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and style (neutral, deft, or over-repressed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone matters: a 'deft hand in a neutral style, somewhat over-repressed perhaps, but thoroughly successful in the achievement of what [the author] set out to do.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether tone matches subject-matter; restraint can be a virtue, but excessive repression may blunt effect. Example: neutral tone may serve reflective war studies; over-repression can reduce immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial stance: identification vs detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the writer identifies with subjects or stands apart affects voice and method ('Where Mr. Dreiser identifies himself with his subjects, Mr. O'Higgins stands apart in the most strict detachment').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate which stance better serves the material. Detachment can reveal patterns and irony; identification can create empathy and immediacy. Anti-pattern: a stance that contradicts the story's ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of departure: small incidents with large consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that begin from 'some tiny and apparently insignificant happening which altered the whole course of a life' are a valid structural choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how plausibly the small incident is shown to alter life and whether the narrative convincingly traces consequences. Look for controlled cause-effect and credible psychological logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of presentation and deliberate looseness of structure
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparently loose structure can conceal 'a new and interesting method of presentation which is as effective as it is deliberate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between deliberate episodic/loose design and mere sloppiness. Re-reading may reveal structural method. Anti-pattern: looseness that masks underprepared plotting or unclear focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense and relentlessness of plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Relentless plotting that exploits human weakness can create high suspense ('inevitable relentlessness of plot based on human weakness').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure cumulative tension, inevitability, and ethical weight of the plot. Good suspense is earned by character psychology and escalation; anti-pattern is sensationalism without depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fertility of imagination matched to worthy material
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's 'wild fertility of imagination' must be put to worthy material; otherwise promise is wasted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether imaginative invention is harnessed to themes and characters that justify it. Excessive fancy on trivial subjects can undermine reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of emotion and sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulty and virtue of 'writing a story so deftly touched with sentiment, while maintaining the necessary economy of personal emotion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize restraint—avoid overwrought or gratuitous emotion. Antipattern: sentimentality in place of genuine feeling. Examples: successful stories touch sentiment lightly yet memorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot technique (competence and originality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical handling of plot—its coherence and inventiveness ('handling of plot leaves little to be desired' or 'entirely mechanical' when weak).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge plot for organic development, surprise consistent with character, and technical control. Mechanical plots betray formula; strong plots feel inevitable yet unpredictable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization and rendering of character
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and truthfulness in rendering character: works may be 'uncertain in its rendering of character' or create 'definitely perceived character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how characters are revealed (action, dialogue, interiority) and whether they are credible and distinct. Anti-patterns: flat or sketchy figures; over-idealized or caricatured portraits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should avoid descending into sentimentality even when they are studies in sentiment ('successfully avoid sentimentality for the most part').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for precise detail and control that preserve feeling from mawkishness. If sentiment feels imposed rather than earned, consider it an artistic failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and focus of a collection
rubrics_metrics.description: A volume often 'would have gained in authority had it been confined' or more tightly focused; unity of selection matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collections, editorial decisions (which pieces to include, whether to group similar stories) affect coherence and authority. Anti-pattern: scattershot collections that dilute an author's best work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concealment of craft (technique visible vs invisible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an author 'conceals the technique of his art'—visible technique can make stories feel less successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise subtle technique that serves the story; critique overt technique that calls attention to itself. Example: Huxley sometimes fails to conceal technique, weakening effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical versus inspired stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stories are 'entirely mechanical' and do not rise above mediocrity; others show living invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish formulaic devices from genuine imaginative solutions. Mechanical plotting, stock characters, and predictable contrivances signal weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness in retelling tradition and folk material
rubrics_metrics.description: Retelling old tales can be successful if done 'in the language of the roads' so that ancient material feels fresh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess voice, immediacy, and cultural authenticity when reworking traditional material. Anti-pattern: stale repetition of folk motifs without new perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of preciosity in impressionistic sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: Impressionistic sketches risk a 'certain preciosity' which good writers must evade to retain authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value simplicity and fidelity to perception over ornate affectation. Evaluate whether impressionism illuminates character and scene rather than ornamenting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of literary medium to author's gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'instinctive dramatist' may be using the wrong medium—the story versus the play question ('whether an instinctive dramatist is using the wrong literary medium').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider if a writer's strengths (dramatic finality, scene-making, dialogue) are better expressed in another form; mismatch can blunt effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propagandist intention versus art
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces written with 'a frankly propagandist intention' can still have vivid portraiture and lasting force, though they may disclaim artistic pretension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh rhetorical purpose against artistic merits: strong portraiture and passion can grant works endurance even if overtly polemical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial curation and collection structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors' choices and imposed structures (e.g., Decameron frame) affect outcome; careless curation shows ('editor will choose his contributors more carefully' and 'abandon the Decameron structure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether framing devices and selection improve or undermine the individual pieces. Anti-pattern: artificial structures appended after stories are written.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation quality and its impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of translation materially affects perceived value ('wretchedly translated' or praise for faithful elegant translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fidelity, tone, and stylistic resonance of translations. Poor translations can mask an author's art; good translations can reveal it. Consider recommending re-edition or alternate translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentation with form and coherence without conventional plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that 'have no plot, no climax, no direct characterization' can nonetheless form a coherent unity 'woven around the spiritual relations' of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conventional elements are absent, look for other organizing principles (theme, mood, spiritual unity). Experimental form is defensible if internally coherent and revealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical polish and finish
rubrics_metrics.description: A finished technical control ('finish unsurpassed in its kind') is a mark of quality in stories and collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sentence-level craft, pacing, and closure. Strong technical finish can redeem weaker material; lack of finish suggests revisionary needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric values and use of setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective short stories can be 'fine studies in atmospheric values' where mood and environment carry weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how sensory detail, tone, and setting contribute to meaning. Atmosphere should arise from precise detail rather than generic description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of revelation: dialogue versus authorial statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Some authors 'achieve his revelation through dialogue rather than personal statement,' a distinct method of character disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the dominant means of revelation: show through dialogue/action or tell through narration. Prefer show (dialogue) when it yields more immediate character truth; beware of heavy-handed authorial summarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentimentality redeemed by technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Works may be mawkish in content yet 'redeemed by excellent technique'—technique can mitigate sentimental weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether craft (voice, pacing, detail) rescues sentimental material. If technique cannot compensate, sentimentality becomes a liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market influence and compromise with audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Compromise with a large audience or market (e.g., writing with an 'eye on the object' for a magazine) can diminish critical standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to work tailored to popular consumption at the expense of artistic challenge. Distinguish sincere popular storytelling from pandering that flattens invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise and potential (developmental value)
rubrics_metrics.description: A volume can be judged valuable for the 'promise' it shows—the author's potential for future growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance present flaws against indications of future achievement; identify memorable pieces as signs of development to come.
